# SetCameraBuffer

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Cameras](Blitz3D-Cameras)

</div>


```blitzbasic
SetCameraBuffer:Void camera:Int32, buffer:Int32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `camera` | In | Int32 | required | Camera handle. |
| `buffer` | In | Int32 | required | The buffer to draw into, or 0 for the buffer of SetBuffer. |

## Description

Makes a camera always draw into one buffer, whatever [SetBuffer](SetBuffer) says. [RenderWorld](RenderWorld) then draws this camera into its own buffer and every other camera into the current buffer, in the usual [EntityOrder](EntityOrder). This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

The buffer can be `BackBuffer()`, `FrontBuffer()` or the [TextureBuffer](TextureBuffer) of a texture made with flag 4096 (render target). An image buffer is not allowed, as with RenderWorld. 0 makes the camera draw into the buffer of SetBuffer again.

[CameraViewport](CameraViewport) is in the buffer the camera draws to, so the default viewport covers the whole texture. When the texture is freed, the camera goes back to the buffer of SetBuffer.

It is meant for things like a security monitor, a rear-view mirror or a minimap: one RenderWorld draws the main view and the texture that a screen in the world shows.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
main = CreateCamera()
PositionEntity main, 0, 0, -5
screen = CreateCube()
monitor = CreateTexture(128, 128, 1 + 4096)
EntityTexture screen, monitor
spy = CreateCamera()
PositionEntity spy, 0, 5, -5
PointEntity spy, screen
SetCameraBuffer spy, TextureBuffer(monitor)
RenderWorld ; The main camera draws into the back buffer, the spy camera into the texture.
Flip
```
